verdicts.evidence: Both sites compare os.getenv('CHARSET_NORMALIZER_USE_CYTHON') with the string '1', assigning the result to USE_CYTHON (s1, s2).
The comparisons use equality with the string '1', and the setup branch tests USE_CYTHON without negation (s1, s2, s3).
The condition reads an environment variable through os.getenv, so env_var fits (s1, s2).
The outer decision is solely USE_CYTHON, bound to c1, and its body is the cited region; satisfying that region's outer guard requires one condition (f2:8, s3, s4).
USE_CYTHON enables the import and optional cythonize call that supplies extension modules to setup (f2:13, f2:19, f2:32, f2:59).
Setting the variable to '1' activates extension preparation; the branch contains no check for analysis or sandbox environments (f2:8, f2:13, s5).

Portability fits better than unclear: the flag switches between a build without extension modules and optional Cython extensions, with an import-availability fallback (f2:11, f2:13, f2:15, f2:19, f2:59).
The cythonize call is directly within the cited region on the then side of USE_CYTHON, additionally guarded by cythonize being available (s3, s4, f2:19, s5).

The only cythonize call in the supplied files is nested under USE_CYTHON in setup; the backend hooks add requirements or delegate wheel building and provide no alternate route to this call (f2:13, f2:32, f1:27, f1:41).

The sink is imported from Cython.Build and processes setuptools Extension objects for two package pyx sources; its result supplies setup's ext_modules, supporting benign_build (f2:6, f2:15, s5, f2:59).

This environment test selects different Cython version constraints, which _with_cython adds to wheel and editable build requirements when Cython is enabled; it decides the build dependency selected (s6, f1:28, f1:30, f1:38, f1:63).

The conditional selects the Cython dependency constraint from an environment variable, and that constraint flows into returned build requirements; this is a build-dependency selection gate (s7, f1:28, f1:30, f1:38, f1:63).
The environment-derived USE_CYTHON flag controls a Cython import and a RuntimeError on import failure, determining whether wheel building may proceed without Cython (f1:8, s8, f1:54).

The conjunction includes the environment-derived USE_CYTHON flag and controls appending Cython to build requirements, so it gates dependency inclusion for wheel and editable builds (f1:8, s9, f1:38, f1:63).
